# Metaframe Editor — complete reference

> An embeddable code and text editor (Monaco, the engine behind VS Code) configured entirely by its
> URL. The document and every editor option are encoded in the URL hash, so one URL is a complete,
> shareable, embeddable editor. No install, no build step, no bundler, no account, no API key.

Base URL: `https://editor.mtfm.io/`
Source:   https://github.com/metapages/metaframe-editor

This document is self-contained. If you are an agent wiring this into a page, everything you need
is below.


## 1. The 30-second version

```html
<iframe src="https://editor.mtfm.io/#?text=SGVsbG8lMkMlMjB3b3JsZCE=&amp;options=JTdCJTIybW9kZSUyMiUzQSUyMm1hcmtkb3duJTIyJTdE"
        style="width:100%;height:400px;border:0"></iframe>
```

That renders a markdown editor containing `Hello, world!`.

The URL shape is always:

```
https://editor.mtfm.io/#?text=<ENCODED_TEXT>&options=<ENCODED_JSON>
```

Everything after `#` is a fragment, so it never reaches a server. The document lives in the link.


## 2. Encoding (read this part carefully)

Both `text` and `options` use the same encoding: **URI-encode the string, then base64 it.**

```js
const encode = (s) => btoa(encodeURIComponent(s));
```

Build a URL:

```js
const encode = (s) => btoa(encodeURIComponent(s));

function editorUrl(text, options = {}) {
  const params = [`text=${encode(text)}`];
  if (Object.keys(options).length) params.push(`options=${encode(JSON.stringify(options))}`);
  return `https://editor.mtfm.io/#?${params.join("&")}`;
}

editorUrl("print('hi')", { mode: "python", theme: "vs-dark" });
```

Node.js (no `btoa` needed):

```js
const encode = (s) => Buffer.from(encodeURIComponent(s)).toString("base64");
```

Python:

```python
import base64, json, urllib.parse

def encode(s: str) -> str:
    return base64.b64encode(urllib.parse.quote(s, safe="").encode()).decode()

def editor_url(text: str, options: dict | None = None) -> str:
    parts = [f"text={encode(text)}"]
    if options:
        parts.append(f"options={encode(json.dumps(options, separators=(',', ':')))}")
    return "https://editor.mtfm.io/#?" + "&".join(parts)
```

All three produce byte-identical output.

### Do not use bare base64

Older examples show `btoa(text)` without the URI-encode step. That is wrong and fails in two ways:

| Input text        | `btoa(text)`                        | `btoa(encodeURIComponent(text))` |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `plain ascii`     | works                               | works                            |
| `50% done`        | **editor shows nothing** (URIError) | works                            |
| `a%20b`           | **silently becomes `a b`**          | works                            |
| `héllo 😀`        | **throws InvalidCharacterError**    | works                            |

Any `%` in your text, and any character outside Latin-1, breaks the bare form. The reader decodes
with `decodeURIComponent(atob(value))` whenever the decoded bytes contain a `%`, so bare base64 of
text containing `%` is misinterpreted. Always URI-encode first. It is also correct for plain ASCII,
so there is never a reason to use the bare form.

### Decoding (reading a URL back)

```js
const decode = (s) => {
  while (s.endsWith("%3D")) s = s.slice(0, -3);   // tolerate over-escaped padding
  const d = atob(s);
  return d.includes("%") ? decodeURIComponent(d) : d;
};
```

### Transport notes

- Base64 `+`, `/` and `=` are legal in a URL fragment. Do not percent-encode them again.
- In an HTML attribute, write the separator as `&amp;` rather than a bare `&`.
- Practical URL ceiling is tens of kilobytes. For large documents, pass the text over the live
  input pipe (section 6) instead of baking it into the URL.


## 3. Hash parameters

Only three parameters are read by this app.

| Param     | Encoding                    | Meaning |
|-----------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `text`    | `base64(uriEncode(string))` | The document body. |
| `options` | `base64(uriEncode(json))`   | Editor configuration, see section 4. |
| `hm`      | plain string                | Menu bar behaviour, see below. |

`hm` controls the hamburger toggle that reveals the Editor / Options / Help tab bar. The tab bar is
hidden by default when the page is inside an iframe, and shown when it is loaded top-level.

| `hm` value            | Behaviour when the menu is toggled off |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------|
| unset or `invisible`  | Hamburger is invisible but still clickable (default). |
| `visible`             | Hamburger stays visible. |
| `disabled`            | No menu at all; cannot be re-opened without editing the URL. Use for a locked-down embed. |

Ignore `button` and `menuhidden` if you see them in older examples — this app does not read them.


## 4. Options

`options` is a JSON object, encoded as in section 2. Every key is optional.

| Key                               | Type                   | Default  | Effect |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------|----------|--------|
| `mode`                            | string (language id)   | `json`   | Syntax highlighting. Any Monaco language id, see section 5. A file extension such as `py` is mapped to its language where unambiguous. |
| `theme`                           | `light` \| `vs-dark`   | `light`  | Colour theme. |
| `readOnly`                        | boolean                | `false`  | Display only; no editing. |
| `saveloadinhash`                  | boolean                | `false`  | Persist edits back into the URL hash (debounced 500 ms), so the URL stays current as the user types. |
| `wordWrap`                        | boolean                | `false`  | Wrap long lines. |
| `hideLineNumbers`                 | boolean                | `false`  | Hide the line-number gutter. |
| `autoFocus`                       | boolean                | `false`  | Focus the editor on load. Avoid on pages with several embeds. |
| `blockLocalEditorStateOverwrites` | boolean                | `false`  | Once the user has typed, ignore incoming input-pipe values so their work is not clobbered. |

Notes:

- With `mode: "json"`, a value that starts with `{` or `[` is `JSON.parse`d before being emitted, so
  downstream consumers receive a real object rather than a string. Invalid JSON is passed through as
  text rather than erroring.
- **There is no Save button.** An edit is emitted on the output pipe as it is made, and written
  into the URL as well when `saveloadinhash` is set. Nothing has to be pressed for an edit to
  count, which matters because this frame is usually embedded in a page that gives no hint a
  press is owed.
- `autosend` was the opt-in to sending on every keystroke, back when the alternative was a Save
  button. It is still accepted in a URL and ignored: sending is now the only behaviour.

Common combinations:

```js
// Static, non-editable code sample on a docs page
{ mode: "python", theme: "vs-dark", readOnly: true, hideLineNumbers: true }

// Live two-way editor that keeps the URL in sync
{ mode: "yaml", saveloadinhash: true }

// Prose scratchpad
{ mode: "plaintext", wordWrap: true }
```


## 5. Language ids for `mode`

90 ids are registered:

```
abap aes apex azcli bat bicep c cameligo clojure coffeescript cpp csharp csp css cypher dart
dockerfile ecl elixir flow9 freemarker2 fsharp go graphql handlebars hcl html ini java javascript
json julia kotlin less lexon liquid lua m3 markdown mdx mips msdax mysql objective-c pascal
pascaligo perl pgsql php pla plaintext postiats powerquery powershell proto pug python qsharp r
razor redis redshift restructuredtext ruby rust sb scala scheme scss shell sol sparql sql st swift
systemverilog tcl twig typescript vb verilog wgsl xml yaml
```

Plus six `freemarker2.tag-*.interpolation-*` variants.

Watch the spellings: `cpp` not `c++`, `csharp` not `cs`, `shell` not `bash`, `proto` not `protobuf`,
`sol` for Solidity, `objective-c` with the hyphen, `plaintext` for no highlighting.

The authoritative live list is the dropdown in the app's Options tab.


## 6. Live data in and out (embedding with two-way flow)

When embedded, the editor talks to its host over `postMessage` using the metaframe protocol. It
declares one input pipe and one output pipe, both named `text` (see `/metaframe.json`).

- **Input**: send a value on the `text` pipe to load it into the editor. If you send a different
  pipe name, the first key received becomes the active name and is used for output too.
- **Output**: the edited value is emitted on the same pipe name, on every keystroke.
- Input values may be a string, a plain object or Blob (stringified to JSON with 2-space indent),
  or a dataref (fetched and read as text). You do not have to pre-serialize.

React, using the convenience wrapper:

```jsx
import { MetaframeStandaloneComponent } from "@metapages/metapage-embed-react";

const encode = (s) => btoa(encodeURIComponent(s));
const options = encode(JSON.stringify({ mode: "python" }));

export const CodeEditor = ({ code, onChange }) => (
  <MetaframeStandaloneComponent
    url={`https://editor.mtfm.io/#?options=${options}&hm=disabled`}
    inputs={{ text: code }}
    onOutputs={(outputs) => onChange(outputs.text)}
  />
);
```

A plain `<iframe>` works identically; the wrapper only saves you the `postMessage` plumbing.

In a metapage, wire any upstream metaframe's output into this one's `text` input and consume its
`text` output downstream — no code at all.


## 7. Gotchas

1. **The hash is read once, at load.** Mutating `iframe.contentWindow.location.hash` on an
   already-loaded embed does not change the content. Set the `src` attribute afresh (or reload) to
   swap documents via URL, or use the input pipe for live updates.
2. **Bare `btoa` corrupts text.** See section 2.
3. **`%3D` padding is tolerated** on read, but emit plain `=` padding.
4. **Without `saveloadinhash`, edits do not update the URL.** The URL keeps the text it was opened
   with, and edits travel only on the output pipe. That is usually what you want for an embed; set
   the flag when the URL should be the user's saveable artifact.
5. **`autoFocus` on several embeds** on one page will fight over focus.
6. **Large documents belong on the input pipe**, not in the URL.


## 8. Machine-readable endpoints

| URL                                     | Contents |
|-----------------------------------------|----------|
| `https://editor.mtfm.io/llms.txt`       | Short index for agents. |
| `https://editor.mtfm.io/llms-full.txt`  | This document. |
| `https://editor.mtfm.io/README.md`      | Human-oriented guide, also shown in the Help tab. |
| `https://editor.mtfm.io/metaframe.json` | Manifest: declared input/output pipes and hash params. |

All are served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so they are fetchable from anywhere.
